drafts.title: Voice assistant recognizes common driving commands reliably while driving
drafts.description: When driving the user can speak common commands (navigation, climate, phone, media) and the car executes them without repeating or manual corrections.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In driving conditions (engine on, cabin noise up to 70 dB) the voice assistant correctly recognizes and executes at least 90% of a validated set of 50 common driving-related commands in a test of 100 utterances per command.
assumptions: A validated corpus of the 50 most common driving commands can be assembled from field data.
Onboard or connected speech models and compute available at successor launch to reach the stated accuracy.
uncertainties: Performance may vary with strong regional accents, heavy background music, or unusual cabin noise not covered by the test.
Some functionality may depend on network availability for cloud-based language models.

drafts.title: Wireless charging pad reliably maintains charging during normal driving
drafts.description: When a phone is placed on the vehicle wireless pad it remains charging during typical drives and recovers quickly from brief interruptions without user intervention.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Across a standardized 30-minute driving session and the top 10 phone models by US registrations at launch, the wireless charger maintains a charging state for at least 95% of sessions and any brief interruptions recover automatically within 10 seconds in at least 95% of occurrences.
assumptions: Test uses common OEM phone cases (up to 3 mm thickness) and standard phone placements as in-field customers use.
Top 10 phone models are known and available at time of validation.
uncertainties: Third‑party magnetic accessories, thick metal cases or non-standard phone placements may still cause failures.
Future phone form factors may require pad redesigns.

drafts.title: HUD and center display remain readable in bright sunlight without user shading
drafts.description: Critical information on the head-up display and the center screen (speed, next navigation cue, primary UI states) is readable by the driver in direct midday sunlight without having to use hand or visor shading.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In an outdoor usability test at direct midday sunlight, 95% of participants can read critical HUD elements (speed and next navigation cue) and primary center-screen UI elements within 3 seconds while seated normally and without using sun visors or hand shading.
assumptions: Usability test uses a representative sample of 50 participants with normal vision and typical seating positions.
Test conditions defined as direct sunlight typical for midday in the target market.
uncertainties: Extreme reflective materials in the cabin, aftermarket window films, or unusual seating positions may reduce readability for some users.
Very small-text UI elements may still require redesign for perfect legibility.

drafts.title: Physical, tactile climate controls operable by touch for temperature and fan
drafts.description: Drivers can change temperature and fan speed by feel without looking at the controls.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In blind-touch trials, drivers can change cabin temperature by at least 1°C and select among fan speed settings within 3 seconds by feel, succeeding in at least 95% of trials across a 40-user panel.
assumptions: Climate UI exposes at least 5 fan speed discrete settings and temperature in 0.5–1°C steps.
Control layout and tactile cues are consistent across trims.
uncertainties: Gloved hands or bulky winter clothing may reduce tactile precision for some users.
Future HVAC feature changes could require control re-mapping.

drafts.title: Heated steering wheel included as part of the cold‑weather package
drafts.description: When customers select the cold‑weather (winter) package in the configurator or at dealers the heated steering wheel is clearly listed as included content.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In the online configurator and dealer configurator test, 95% of users can confirm that the cold‑weather package includes the heated steering wheel within 30 seconds; the package listing explicitly shows the heated steering wheel as included.
assumptions: Packaging decisions (package content lists) are aligned across sales channels at launch.
Regional package names may vary but include the heated steering wheel in market-specific cold-weather packages.
uncertainties: Some regional markets may regulate package contents differently, requiring local variation.
Dealer-level options or retrofit availability may differ from configurator content.

drafts.title: Heated seats can be purchased and activated via an in‑vehicle subscription flow
drafts.description: Drivers can buy and activate heated seat functionality from inside the car without visiting a dealer, and the seats heat up after activation.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: A driver can complete purchase and activation of a heated‑seats subscription entirely inside the vehicle within 120 seconds and the seat heating becomes active within 2 minutes in at least 95% of test activations.
assumptions: In‑vehicle payment integration and regional commerce agreements are available at launch in the test market.
Activation APIs for seat heaters are available to the subscription flow.
uncertainties: Legal or payment method restrictions in certain regions may prevent instant in‑vehicle purchases.
Offline activations (no network) may require alternate flows or delay activation.

drafts.title: Regulatory and data‑protection certification requests (out of scope)
drafts.description: Customers request that the infotainment system satisfy country certification (e.g., CCC) and data‑protection (GDPR) requirements. These items are regulatory/compliance requests and are out of scope for product outcome requirements.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Out of scope: regulatory and certification activities are handled by BMW compliance and legal teams; product teams will receive certification status as assumptions for implementation.
assumptions: Regulatory certification and legal approvals will be obtained by the compliance organization as required for each market.
uncertainties: Timing and exact requirements for certifications may change and affect feature availability in some markets.
drafts.scope_reason: Regulation/certification and legal compliance are handled by compliance teams and are out of scope for customer-facing product requirement definitions.

drafts.title: Request for a specific cockpit processor (engineering spec, out of scope)
drafts.description: Customers asked that the cockpit computer use a specific chip. Requests for particular hardware components are engineering specifications and are out of scope for customer-facing requirements.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Out of scope: choice of specific processor is an engineering-level specification to be evaluated by the platform and systems teams.
assumptions: Platform teams will assess available SoC options balancing performance, power and lifecycle at the time of design.
uncertainties: Supply chain availability and vendor roadmaps may influence final hardware choices.
drafts.scope_reason: Engineering specification (request for a particular chip) — not a customer-facing outcome.

drafts.title: Pricing, discounts, leasing and dealer margin requests (out of scope)
drafts.description: Customers asked for lower base price, cheaper leases, package discounts, lower dealer margins and 0% financing. These are pricing and commercial requests and therefore out of scope for product requirements.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Out of scope: pricing, financing and dealer margin decisions fall under commercial and pricing strategy and are not converted into technical customer-facing requirements here.
assumptions: Commercial and regional pricing strategies will be set by BMW Sales & Marketing and Finance teams.
uncertainties: Market conditions and competitor actions can influence final pricing/financing offers available to customers.
drafts.scope_reason: Price, financing and dealer margin requests are commercial decisions and out of scope for technical/product requirements.
